ledger.x: 889: Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Saj takes up the governorship of Azerbaijan at Maragha.
901: Yusuf overthrows his nephew and moves the capital to Ardabil.
909: Yusuf takes Nakhichevan and shares Siunikh.
c. 909: the Shirvanshah becomes dependent on the Sajids. 'the Sajids made the Shirvanshah Mazyadids dependent on them' (908-909 to 919, per Bakikhanov); the page does not use the word vassal.
c. 909: Gagik Artsruni of Vaspurakan becomes Yusuf's vassal 'after a dispute with the Bagratids over Nakhichevan'; the page gives no year, so the start is bridged from the 909 Nakhichevan campaign.
After 917: Yusuf conquers Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray.
929: the Artsruni tie lapses with the end of the dynasty.
929: the last Sajid is poisoned and the dynasty ends.

wars.name: Sajid–Abbasid conflict of 908–909
wars.outcome: A caliphal army was sent in 908; al-Muqtadir made peace and invested Yusuf with Azerbaijan and Armenia in 909 for a tribute of 120 thousand dinars a year; Yusuf stopped paying after 912.

wars.name: Sajid campaigns in Armenia
wars.outcome: Nakhichevan taken in 909; Smbat's sons beaten north of Erevan in 910; Smbat trapped in a fortress about 913 and later executed; Gagik Artsruni a vassal.

wars.name: Sajid campaign in Georgia
wars.outcome: Yusuf campaigned in Georgian territories with Tiflis as his base; no lasting hold recorded.

wars.name: Sajid conquest of Ray and its neighbours
wars.outcome: Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray taken after 917; Ray retaken in 924.

wars.name: Sajid–Qarmatian campaign
wars.outcome: The caliph ordered Yusuf against al-Hasa in 926; his army was defeated near Kufa in 927 and he was killed in 928.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the Sajid frontiers in the Caucasus, the Araxes valley and the Ray edge are approximate.
